newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vote paves way for sale of German utility Bewag.
newsitem.headline: Vote paves way for sale of German utility Bewag.

text.p: Government officials late on Tuesday voted in favour of full privatisation of state utility group Berliner Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag), in which several German and foreign firms have shown interest.

A special conference of Berlin's Social Democrats (SPD), who govern Berlin in coalition with the Christian Democrats (CDU), ended with 162 of 288 delegates supporting selling the state's final 25 percent stake in Bewag, an SPD spokesman said.
Although the decision must be approved in parliament, it has cleared the way for Bewag to be privatised in full.
The state currently owns 50.8 percent of Bewag and has been negotiating since last year to sell a 25.8 percent package.
Utilities Bayernwerk, a unit of Viag AG, and Preussenelektra, owned by Veba AG, each hold a further 10 percent in the company and the remainder is held by smaller shareholders.
Viag AG has confirmed it is interested in increasing the stake and industry sources said last December that it planned to make a joint bid with Veba for a higher stake.
Several other companies, among them foreign firms, are also reported to be interested in the company.
